attacks.claim: Buying the county voter file and sending automated SMS to ~142,000 people with no consent basis is a bulk unsolicited text campaign. TCPA exposure is severe ($500–$1,500 per message), the file's permitted-use terms are unchecked, and the plan contradicts the anonymous-first, optional-verification constraint.
attacks.evidence: "Purchase the county voter registration file from the County Clerk ($400, includes mobile numbers where provided). Load numbers into Twilio and send an automated SMS to every registered voter in the city (~142,000)" ABSENT: consent basis, permitted-use review, opt-in gate.

attacks.claim: The weekly public CC-BY CSV publishes ward, zip, birth_year, gender, ranking and verified per response with no k-anonymity, small-cell suppression, or review step. Combined quasi-identifiers allow re-identification, and a public CC-BY release cannot be recalled once downloaded.
attacks.evidence: "one CSV per poll on data.ourtown.org with columns ward, zip, birth_year, gender, ranking, verified, created_at. resident_id is removed before export." ABSENT: suppression threshold or retraction path.

attacks.claim: Verified residents' address, zip, birth_year and gender sit alongside ranking responses, and the plan provides no resident deletion or erasure process. Staff cannot delete responses, so a person's data cannot be removed on request.
attacks.evidence: "Verified residents already have address, zip, birth_year, gender" and "Staff cannot edit or delete responses" ABSENT: erasure or deletion process for residents and poll_responses.

attacks.claim: The anti-brigading guarantee is asserted without evidence. Device-fingerprint and per-IP limits are easily rotated or spoofed, and the plan has no abuse test or threat model supporting the claim that brigades cannot masquerade as verified sentiment.
attacks.evidence: "so a brigade of unverified responses cannot masquerade as verified sentiment" ABSENT: abuse test or threat analysis for fingerprint/IP limits.

attacks.claim: The one-per-device-fingerprint limit cannot be enforced as written. poll_responses has no fingerprint column or unique index, and the one-per-verified-resident rule is a check-then-insert race. A Postgres unique constraint also does not cover unverified rows because NULL resident_id values are distinct.
attacks.evidence: "poll_responses(id, poll_id, resident_id null, ranking jsonb, ward, verified bool, created_at)" ABSENT: fingerprint field, unique index, or locking strategy.

attacks.claim: The plan does not say how the verified flag and verified-resident ward are set server-side. Unverified users self-select ward and submit ranking JSON, and neither is validated against poll options or the ward list. Client-supplied values could distort the split tallies and flow into the public CSV and staff PDF.
attacks.evidence: "ward is self-selected for unverified users" and "ranking jsonb" ABSENT: server-side derivation rule for verified, and validation of ranking and ward values.

attacks.claim: The IRV tally is underspecified. It does not define partial-ranking validity, exhausted-ballot handling, or tie-breaks. It also does not say whether winners are computed per ward or citywide, and those can differ on the same poll.
attacks.evidence: "Residents rank options; results are shown per ward with instant-runoff tallies." ABSENT: partial-ranking rule, tie/exhaustion rule, and which scope drives the outcome.

attacks.claim: Responses placed in the rate-limit review queue have no defined state. It is unclear whether they count in tallies, and because staff cannot edit or delete responses, queued items may never be resolved.
attacks.evidence: "unverified responses over 3/min from one IP are queued for review" alongside "Staff cannot edit or delete responses."

attacks.claim: The outreach reach math is wrong. Mobile numbers are included only where provided, so the SMS pipeline cannot reach all ~142,000 registered voters, and the plan never states the reachable count.
attacks.evidence: "includes mobile numbers where provided" and "send an automated SMS to every registered voter in the city (~142,000)"

attacks.claim: The 142k SMS pipeline has no retry, idempotency, send-status tracking, throttling, or bounce handling. A partial failure leaves no defined way to resume, detect failures, or avoid duplicate reminders.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retry/backoff, idempotency, send-status tracking, alerting. "Load numbers into Twilio and send an automated SMS to every registered voter in the city (~142,000)"

attacks.claim: There is no kill switch or pause for the 3 reminders, and no suppression of residents who already responded or opted out. Once messages go out to 142k people they cannot be recalled, and spend keeps accruing even when the poll is broken.
attacks.evidence: "then 3 automated reminders over 10 days" ABSENT: pause/cancel mechanism, responder suppression, budget stop condition.

attacks.claim: The SMS campaign has no budget or cost estimate, although ~142k messages plus 3 reminders each is roughly 568k messages. Twilio spend is never estimated or capped before launch.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: per-message cost, total SMS budget, hard spend cap. "send an automated SMS to every registered voter in the city (~142,000)... then 3 automated reminders over 10 days"

attacks.claim: No capacity plan exists for the link-click and STOP-reply spike from ~568k messages on the self-hosted Django/Postgres stack, or for IRV recomputation on the live results page. The 5k-concurrent load target is not tied to any results query plan or caching strategy.
attacks.evidence: "Live results page: instant-runoff rounds" and "load test (target 5k concurrent)" ABSENT: IRV compute strategy (on-request vs cached), send pacing, link-spike capacity estimate.

attacks.claim: Self-hosted Postgres has no backup, restore, or DR plan, yet poll responses are irreplaceable and cannot be edited or deleted by staff. A data loss event would be unrecoverable.
attacks.evidence: "self-hosted on the org's existing servers" and "Staff cannot edit or delete responses" ABSENT: backup, restore, or DR plan.

attacks.claim: There is no observability, alerting, or on-call plan for a public civic system with launch and budget-hearing spikes. Failed weekly exports or the Monday 07:00 staff email would fail silently, leaving stale public data and staff unaware the summary never arrived.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: monitoring, alerting, SLOs, retry for "weekly, public, CC-BY" export and "emailed Monday 07:00" PDF.

attacks.claim: Resident mobile numbers and verified demographics leave the self-hosted infrastructure for Twilio with no residency, retention, or deletion terms, and no alternative delivery path or exit plan. This creates single-vendor lock-in for the core launch channel.
attacks.evidence: "Load numbers into Twilio and send an automated SMS to every registered voter" ABSENT: Twilio data-residency, retention, deletion terms, or exit path.

attacks.claim: Staff receive resident-level CSVs with zip, birth_year and gender, plus an emailed PDF outside app controls. There is no role-based access, audit trail, or minimization for this personal data.
attacks.evidence: "Council staff get the same CSV plus a PDF summary emailed Monday 07:00." ABSENT: role-based access, audit log, recipient limits.

attacks.claim: Retention and hashing are unstated for device fingerprints and IP addresses used in rate limiting, and for verified residents' address, birth_year and gender. These are personal data with no retention schedule.
attacks.evidence: "1 response per poll per device fingerprint" and "from one IP" ABSENT: retention and hashing rules for fingerprints/IPs and verified fields.

attacks.claim: Demographic data collected for jury-pool balance reports is reused for ward assignment and public CC-BY export without stated notice, purpose limitation, or consent change, which may breach the disclosures under which it was collected.
attacks.evidence: "collected at optional verification for the jury-pool-style demographic balance reports" and "one CSV per poll on data.ourtown.org"

attacks.claim: The product case conflicts with the survey. Polls on upcoming items got 9% of selections, while council voting records and reasons got 61%, yet Ward Voice is called the 'centerpiece' and the success metrics (6,000 responses, 30% new residents) have no stated basis.
attacks.evidence: "Polls on upcoming items — 9%" vs "Ward Voice ... is the centerpiece of the FY27 roadmap." ABSENT: basis for 6,000 responses or 30% new-resident target.

attacks.claim: The plan never states whether results are advisory or binding, how council receives them, or that the self-selected unverified responses are not representative. Presenting IRV results as a 'direct voice' on council decisions risks misrepresenting public opinion in a public record, and no legal or public-records review is documented.
attacks.evidence: "gives residents a direct voice on the items council is actually deciding" ABSENT: how results feed council decisions, representativeness caveat, public-records review.

attacks.claim: Ranking is specified as drag or tap with no keyboard-only or screen-reader requirement, and accessibility is deferred to a single Week 5 pass before launch. Multi-round IRV tables have no accessible markup or non-color encoding, and there is no WCAG target.
attacks.evidence: "resident ranking UI (mobile-first, drag or tap-to-rank)" and "Week 5: accessibility pass" ABSENT: keyboard/SR requirement, WCAG target, accessible table markup.

attacks.claim: The verified and all-responses columns are not labeled for residents. Readers may take the instant-runoff results as representative sentiment, undermining the separation the integrity model relies on.
attacks.evidence: "split into 'verified' and 'all responses' columns" ABSENT: labeling or explanation of which tally is which.

attacks.claim: A mass SMS campaign to voter-file contacts is a major new capability, with purchased data, Twilio import and recurring texts, that is absent from the stated poll feature scope and not designed as a separable module. This couples the product launch to an outreach pipeline.
attacks.evidence: "Purchase the county voter registration file ... Load numbers into Twilio" (Section 6 outside the Section 2 scope).

attacks.claim: Unsolicited SMS to people who never opted into OurTown is likely to read as spam and damage trust in a civic nonprofit, working against the stated goal of meaningful participation. The 30% new-resident metric can be inflated by this outreach without real engagement.
attacks.evidence: "30% of responses from residents not previously active on OurTown." and "send an automated SMS to every registered voter in the city"

attacks.claim: The weekly export and Monday PDF are full-table regenerations with no incremental or streaming design, so cost grows with total responses across all polls.
attacks.evidence: "one CSV per poll on data.ourtown.org" and "PDF summary emailed Monday 07:00" ABSENT: incremental or streaming approach.

attacks.claim: The verified flag and ward are fixed at submission time. Later verification or an address change leaves stale values, so split tallies drift from current resident data.
attacks.evidence: "verified bool" and "derived from address for verified users" ABSENT: update or recompute rule.

attacks.claim: The 30% new-resident success metric cannot be computed because the data model has no prior-activity or first-seen field.
attacks.evidence: "30% of responses from residents not previously active on OurTown." ABSENT: activity or first-seen field in residents or poll_responses.

attacks.claim: The results page has no display spec for IRV elimination rounds, transfers or ties, and the ranking UI has no spec for position numbers or unranked options, so both views risk being misleading or unreadable.
attacks.evidence: "instant-runoff rounds" and "drag or tap-to-rank" ABSENT: display specs for rounds, ties, ranking state.

attacks.claim: Results are computed separately for the live page and the export/PDF, with no shared tally service specified, which invites divergent IRV implementations.
attacks.evidence: "Live results page: instant-runoff rounds" and "Council staff get the same CSV plus a PDF summary"
